questions.question: The Vindhya Range separates which two river systems?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ganga and Narmada**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Vindhya Range** is a vast, discontinuous chain of mountain ridges, highlands, and plateau escarpments in **Central India**, traditionally forming the boundary between **North India** and **South India**.
 
• It acts as a primary **geographical watershed**, a natural divide that separates the drainage basins of the **Ganga River** system in the north from the **Narmada River** system in the south.
 
• The northern slopes of the Vindhyas drain into the **Ganga basin** through tributaries such as the **Chambal**, **Betwa**, **Ken**, and **Son** rivers, which eventually join the **Yamuna** or the **Ganga**.
 
• The **Narmada River** flows through a narrow **rift valley** located immediately south of the Vindhya Range, separating it from the parallel **Satpura Range**.
 
• Historically and geologically, the range has prevented the mixing of the **perennial Himalayan-fed** systems of the north with the **rain-fed peninsular** rivers flowing through the central rift.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Narmada and Tapi**:

 
 
• These are the two major **west-flowing rivers** of India.
 
• They are separated by the **Satpura Range**, which lies between the two river valleys.
 
 
 
• **Satpura Range**:
 
 
• Located south of the **Vindhyas**, it originates in eastern **Gujarat** and runs through **Maharashtra** and **Madhya Pradesh** to **Chhattisgarh**.
 
• It separates the **Narmada** basin from the **Tapi** basin to its south.
 
 
 
• **Godavari and Krishna**:
 
 
• These are the largest **east-flowing rivers** in the **Peninsular Plateau**.
 
• Their basins are separated by the **Balaghat Range** and the **Ajanta Hills** in the **Deccan Plateau** region.
 
 
 
• **Amarkantak Plateau**:
 
 
• This is a significant geological region where the **Vindhya** and **Satpura** ranges meet, serving as the source for the **Narmada**, **Son**, and **Johila** rivers.

questions.question: According to the demographic transition theory, India is presently in which stage of population growth?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Late expanding**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Demographic Transition Model (DTM)** is a framework that describes the historical shift of birth and death rates in societies as they develop economically.
 
• India is currently categorized in **Stage 3**, known as the **Late expanding** stage, characterized by a declining **birth rate** and a low **death rate**.
 
• Statistical data from the **National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5)** confirms that India’s **Total Fertility Rate (TFR)** has fallen to **2.0**, which is below the **replacement level fertility** of 2.1.
 
• While the **mortality rate** has stabilized at a low level due to advancements in **healthcare**, **sanitation**, and **immunization**, the population continues to grow because of **population momentum**.
 
• The decline in birth rates is attributed to factors such as increasing **female literacy**, higher levels of **urbanization**, and widespread awareness of **family planning** methods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Stage 1: High stationary**

 
 
• Characterized by high birth and high death rates, resulting in minimal population growth.
 
• In India, this phase ended around **1921**, which is historically recognized as the **Year of the Great Divide** due to the onset of a consistent decline in mortality.
 
 
 
• **Stage 2: Early expanding**
 
 
• Marked by a high birth rate and a rapidly falling death rate, leading to a **population explosion**.
 
• India navigated this stage between **1921 and 1981**, during which massive improvements in **food security** and **medicine** drastically reduced the death rate.
 
 
 
• **Stage 4: Low stationary**
 
 
• Defined by low birth and low death rates, leading to a stable or slowly growing population.
 
• This stage is typically observed in highly **developed countries** with advanced industrial economies.

questions.question: Which reform is often described as the blueprint for the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Government of India Act, 1935**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Government of India Act, 1935** is considered the **blueprint** of the Indian Constitution because nearly 60 to 70 percent of the current Constitution’s provisions are derived from it.
 
• It was the longest and most detailed act passed by the **British Parliament**, featuring 321 sections and 10 schedules, providing a comprehensive administrative framework for the country.
 
• The Act proposed the establishment of an **All-India Federation** comprising British Indian provinces and **Princely States** as voluntary units.
 
• It introduced **Provincial Autonomy** by abolishing **Diarchy** in the provinces and allowing them to function as autonomous administrative units.
 
• Key structural elements such as the **Federal Scheme**, the **Office of Governor**, **Public Service Commissions**, **Judiciary**, and **Emergency Provisions** were adopted from this Act into the Indian Constitution.
 
• It also established the **Reserve Bank of India** (1935) and a **Federal Court** (1937) to further institutionalize the governance of British India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Morley-Minto Reforms (1909)**:

 
 
• Formally known as the **Indian Councils Act 1909**, it introduced **separate electorates** for Muslims.
 
• It is often criticized for sowing the seeds of **communalism** in Indian politics.
 
 
 
• **Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms (1919)**:
 
 
• Enacted as the **Government of India Act 1919**, it introduced the system of **Diarchy** (rule of two) in the provinces.
 
• It established a **bicameral legislature** at the central level for the first time.
 
 
 
• **Indian Independence Act, 1947**:
 
 
• This act ended **British sovereignty** over India and provided for the creation of two independent dominions: **India** and **Pakistan**.
 
• It abolished the office of the **Secretary of State for India** and the title of **Emperor of India**.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a denomination of notes demonetised in 1978?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**500**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The demonetization of 1978 was officially carried out under the **High Denomination Bank Notes (Demonetisation) Act, 1978**, which came into effect on **January 16, 1978**.
 
• The **Janata Party** coalition government, led by Prime Minister **Morarji Desai**, initiated this move with the primary goal of curbing **black money**, **tax evasion**, and the **shadow economy**.
 
• The specific high-value currency notes that were declared no longer legal tender were the **1,000**, **5,000**, and **10,000** rupee denominations.
 
• The **500** rupee note was **not** demonetized in 1978 because it was not in active circulation at that time. It was reintroduced by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** much later, in **October 1987**, to manage the growing volume of cash transactions and **inflation**.
 
• At the time of the 1978 exercise, **I. G. Patel** served as the **Governor of the Reserve Bank of India**, and the ordinance was issued by the then President **Neelam Sanjiva Reddy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **History of High-Denomination Notes**:

 
 
• **10,000 Rupee Note**: This was the highest denomination ever printed. It was first introduced in **1938**, demonetized in **1946**, reintroduced in **1954**, and finally demonetized again in **1978**.
 
• **5,000 Rupee Note**: Introduced in **1954** along with the 1,000 and 10,000 notes, it remained in circulation until the 1978 demonetization.
 
• **1,000 Rupee Note**: This denomination has been demonetized three times in Indian history (**1946**, **1978**, and **2016**).
 
 
 
• **Other Demonetization Events**:
 
 
• **1946 Demonetization**: The first instance in India, where **500**, **1,000**, and **10,000** rupee notes were withdrawn by the British administration.
 
• **2016 Demonetization**: Occurred on **November 8, 2016**, where the **500** and **1,000** rupee notes were scrapped, representing nearly **86 percent** of the cash in circulation.

questions.question: The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology on January 3, 2025, unveiled the draft rules for implementing the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2023**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act** was officially enacted in **2023** after receiving the **Presidential assent** on **August 11, 2023**.
 
• On **January 3, 2025**, the **Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)** unveiled the much-anticipated **draft rules** to operationalize the provisions of this landmark legislation.
 
• The Act represents India's first dedicated **comprehensive data protection law**, designed to regulate how **Data Fiduciaries** (entities that process data) handle the personal information of **Data Principals** (individuals).
 
• The 2023 framework focuses on the principles of **consent-based processing**, **purpose limitation**, and **data minimization** to ensure digital privacy in an increasingly connected economy.
 
• The draft rules released in **January 2025** provide specific procedures for **grievance redressal**, the functioning of the **Data Protection Board of India**, and the requirements for obtaining **verifiable parental consent** for children's data.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Core Components of the DPDP Act 2023**:

 
 
• **Data Protection Board of India**: An independent regulatory body established to monitor compliance, conduct inquiries, and impose financial penalties.
 
• **Financial Penalties**: The Act prescribes significant penalties for **data breaches** or non-compliance, reaching up to **Rs 250 crore** for specific violations.
 
• **Rights of Data Principals**: Individuals hold the **right to access** information, the **right to correction** and erasure, and the **right to nominate** a person to exercise their rights in case of death or incapacity.
 
• **Duties of Data Fiduciaries**: Organizations must implement **security safeguards**, notify the Board and affected individuals in case of a breach, and appoint a **Data Protection Officer (DPO)** if they are categorized as **Significant Data Fiduciaries**.
 
 
 
• **Evolution from Previous Frameworks**:
 
 
• Before the **2023 Act**, data privacy was primarily governed by the **Information Technology (Reasonable Security Practices and Procedures and Sensitive Personal Data or Information) Rules, 2011**, which were limited in scope.
 
• The **IT Act, 2000** provided the initial legal foundation for electronic governance but lacked the robust protections required for modern **digital personal data**.

questions.question: Which of the following art forms of Kerala is inscribed in the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kutiyattam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kutiyattam**, a Sanskrit theatrical tradition from **Kerala**, is one of India's oldest living art forms, dating back over **2,000 years**.
 
• It was the first Indian art form to be recognized by **UNESCO** as a **Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity** in **2001**, and was later included in the **Representative List** in **2008**.
 
• The performance is traditionally held in **Koothambalams**, which are specialized theaters located within Hindu temple complexes in Kerala.
 
• It is characterized by a unique combination of **Sanskrit drama** and local **Malayalam** stylistic elements, involving highly stylized **Abhinaya** (acting) and complex hand gestures.
 
• The lead male actors belong to the **Chakyar** community, while female roles are performed by the **Nangyiar** community; the **Nambiars** play the **Mizhavu**, a sacred copper percussion instrument.
 
• The repertoire includes plays by celebrated Sanskrit dramatists like **Bhasa**, **Harsha**, and **Mahendra Pallava**, focusing on elaborate character development that can span several nights.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kummi**:

 
 
• A popular folk dance in **Tamil Nadu** and **Kerala**, typically performed by women in a circle.
 
• It relies on **hand-clapping** to maintain rhythm rather than musical instruments, often performed during festivals like **Pongal**.
 
 
 
• **Bagurumba**:
 
 
• A traditional folk dance of the **Bodo tribe** in **Assam**, often called the **Butterfly Dance** due to the dancers mimicking the movement of butterflies.
 
• It is performed during the **Bwisagu** festival in mid-April.
 
 
 
• **Perini Shivatandavam**:
 
 
• A vigorous ancient dance form from **Telangana**, also known as the **Dance of Warriors**.
 
• Originating during the **Kakatiya dynasty**, it was performed by soldiers in front of Lord Shiva's idol before heading to war.

questions.question: According to the universal law of gravitation, what is used to denote the constant of proportionality?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**G**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Universal Law of Gravitation**, formulated by **Sir Isaac Newton** in **1687**, describes the gravitational attraction between two objects possessing **mass**.
 
• This law states that the force of attraction is **directly proportional** to the product of the masses of the two objects and **inversely proportional** to the square of the distance between their centers.
 
• To represent this relationship as an equation, the **constant of proportionality** known as **G** is used.
 
• The mathematical formula is written as **F = G × (m1 × m2) / r²**, where **F** is the gravitational force, **m1** and **m2** are the masses, and **r** is the separation distance.
 
• The symbol **G** is specifically designated as the **Universal Gravitational Constant** because its value is assumed to be the same everywhere in the universe.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Universal Gravitational Constant (G)**:

 
 
• The precise value of **G** is approximately **6.674 × 10−¹¹ N m²/kg²**.
 
• It was first measured accurately by **Henry Cavendish** in **1798** using a sophisticated **torsion balance**.
 
• Unlike **g** (acceleration due to gravity), **G** is a **scalar quantity** and does not change with location.
 
 
 
• **Other Symbols in Physics**:
 
 
• **mu (μ)**: Commonly denotes the **coefficient of friction** between surfaces or **magnetic permeability** in electromagnetism.
 
• **k**: Often represents the **Boltzmann constant** in thermodynamics or the **Coulomb constant** in electrostatics.
 
• **phi (φ)**: Typically signifies **magnetic flux**, the **work function** in quantum mechanics, or a **phase angle** in wave optics.

questions.question: Which of the following is considered as a legal tender?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Coins**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Legal tender** is defined as any form of payment that is recognized by the legal system of a country as valid for the settlement of public or private debts and financial obligations.
 
• In India, **coins** are issued by the **Government of India** under the provisions of the **Coinage Act, 2011**. They are considered a form of **Limited Legal Tender**.
 
• Unlike banknotes, which are liabilities of the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, coins are assets issued directly by the central government. The government determines the denominations, designs, and quantities of coins to be minted at the four **India Government Mints** located in **Mumbai**, **Kolkata**, **Hyderabad**, and **Noida**.
 
• According to **Section 13** of the **Coinage Act, 2011**, coins of any denomination not lower than **one rupee** are legal tender for any sum not exceeding **1,000 rupees**. Coins of **50 paise** are legal tender for any sum up to **10 rupees**.
 
• While the public can use coins for transactions, they are **Limited Legal Tender** because a person cannot be legally forced to accept them beyond the specified statutory limits mentioned in the act.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Debit and Credit Cards**:

 
 
• These are categorized as **Plastic Money**. They facilitate electronic fund transfers but are not **legal tender**.
 
• No individual or merchant is legally bound to accept a **Debit card** or **Credit card** for payment; their use is based on contractual agreements between the merchant, the customer, and the bank.
 
 
 
• **Cheque**:
 
 
• A **cheque** is a type of **Fiduciary Money**, which is money that is accepted as a medium of exchange because of the trust (fides) between the payer and the payee.
 
• It is an order to a bank to pay a specific amount from a person's account. Since it is not **legal tender**, a creditor can legally refuse to accept a **cheque** and insist on payment in currency notes or **coins**.

questions.question: Which of the following is commonly referred to as a "conflict" or "blood" mineral due to its role in financing armed groups in conflict zones specially in Africa?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Diamond**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Conflict diamonds**, popularly known as **blood diamonds**, refer to rough diamonds used by rebel movements or their allies to finance armed conflict aimed at undermining legitimate governments.
 
• The term gained global prominence during the late **1990s** due to brutal civil wars in **African nations** such as **Sierra Leone**, **Angola**, **Liberia**, and the **Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC)**.
 
• To address this crisis, the **United Nations** and various stakeholders established the **Kimberley Process Certification Scheme (KPCS)** in **2003**, which requires member nations to certify that shipments of rough diamonds are **conflict-free**.
 
• Statistical data from the early **2000s** estimated that conflict diamonds accounted for approximately **4 percent** to **15 percent** of the global diamond trade, leading to millions of deaths and displacements.
 
• The **Clean Diamond Trade Act**, passed by the **United States Congress** in **2003**, further strengthened international efforts by prohibiting the import of diamonds from countries not participating in the **Kimberley Process**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cobalt**:

 
 
• Primarily mined in the **Copperbelt** region of the **Democratic Republic of Congo**, which holds over **70 percent** of the world's reserves.
 
• Essential for the production of **lithium-ion batteries** used in **electric vehicles** and **smartphones**.
 
• While not traditionally called a **blood mineral** in the same historical context as diamonds, its extraction is heavily scrutinized for **human rights abuses** and **child labor**.
 
 
 
• **Gypsum**:
 
 
• A common **evaporite mineral** chemically known as **calcium sulfate dihydrate**.
 
• Mainly utilized in the manufacture of **wallboard** (drywall), **cement**, and **fertilizers**.
 
 
 
• **Nickel**:
 
 
• A transition metal primarily found in **laterite** and **magmatic sulfide** deposits.
 
• Key industrial applications include **stainless steel production** and the manufacturing of **rechargeable batteries**.

questions.question: Where was the Rugby Premier League final held in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mumbai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Mumbai** was chosen due to its superior **sporting infrastructure** and long-standing association with rugby, dating back to the establishment of the **Bombay Gymkhana** in **1875**.
 
• The event was organized under the supervision of the **Indian Rugby Football Union (IRFU)**, aiming to boost the commercial viability of the sport through a high-profile metropolitan final.
 
• The 2025 final saw a record attendance for a non-cricket event in the city, highlighting the successful expansion of **Rugby Union** and **Rugby Sevens** across urban centers in India.
 
• Selection of this venue align with the **Maharashtra Government** policy of promoting diverse sports to establish the state as a premier global sporting hub.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Rugby Football Union (IRFU)**:

 
 
• Commonly known as **Rugby India**, it is the sole governing body for the sport in the country and is a full member of **World Rugby** and **Asia Rugby**.
 
• The union has been instrumental in the inclusion of rugby in the **National Games** and the **Khelo India University Games**.
 
 
 
• **Growth of Rugby in India**:
 
 
• India has seen a surge in participation, particularly in the **Rugby Sevens** format, which is an **Olympic** sport.

questions.question: In the mega consolidation in public sector banks in 2020, which of the following banks were merged into Indian Bank?

options.text: Oriental Bank of Commerce and United Bank of India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Allahabad Bank**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On **August 30, 2019**, the **Government of India** announced a massive structural reform involving the consolidation of ten **Public Sector Banks (PSBs)** into four large entities, which officially came into force on **April 1, 2020**.
 
• As a result of this mega consolidation, **Allahabad Bank** was merged with **Indian Bank**, with **Indian Bank** acting as the anchor bank.
 
• The merger transformed **Indian Bank** into the **seventh-largest** public sector bank in India, significantly increasing its nationwide footprint and operational scale.
 
• The combined entity achieved a total business volume of approximately **Rs 8.07 lakh crore** at the time of the merger, benefiting from **Allahabad Bank’s** strong presence in **Northern** and **Eastern India**.
 
• The primary objective behind this consolidation was to create **globally competitive banks** with larger **balance sheets**, improved **capital adequacy**, and enhanced **lending capacity** to support the **5 trillion dollar economy** goal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oriental Bank of Commerce and United Bank of India**:

 
 
• These two banks were amalgamated into **Punjab National Bank (PNB)**, making **PNB** the second-largest state-owned bank in India after **SBI**.
 
 
 
• **Syndicate Bank**:
 
 
• This bank was merged into **Canara Bank**, which resulted in the creation of the fourth-largest **Public Sector Bank** in the country.
 
 
 
• **Andhra Bank and Corporation Bank**:
 
 
• These entities were merged into **Union Bank of India**, elevating its position to the fifth-largest **PSB** by total business.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of PSBs**:
 
 
• The merger process reduced the total number of **Public Sector Banks** from **27** in **2017** to just **12** by **2020**.
 
• Earlier consolidations included the **State Bank of India** merger with its associates in **2017** and the **Bank of Baroda** merger with **Vijaya Bank** and **Dena Bank** in **2019**.

questions.question: In Table tennis, the playing space shall be rectangular and should not be less than ____ metres long.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**14**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the regulations set by the **International Table Tennis Federation (ITTF)**, the playing space for international competitions must be **rectangular**.
 
• The official rules specify that for **World Title** events and **Olympic Games**, the length of the playing space must not be less than **14 metres**.
 
• The **minimum width** of this rectangular playing space is required to be **7 metres** to allow for adequate side-to-side movement during play.
 
• The **minimum height** from the floor to any overhead obstruction must be at least **5 metres**.
 
• These dimensions ensure that high-level athletes have sufficient room to execute advanced maneuvers, such as **lopping** or **defensive play** far from the table, without being restricted by physical barriers.
 
• For other **International Competitions**, the space may be reduced slightly to **12 metres** long and **6 metres** wide, but the standard for top-tier tournaments remains 14 metres.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Table Dimensions**:

 
 
• The standard table is **2.74 metres** long and **1.525 metres** wide.
 
• The playing surface must be **76 centimetres** above the floor and lie in a horizontal plane.
 
 
 
• **Net Assembly**:
 
 
• The net is **15.25 centimetres** high, and its ends must extend **15.25 centimetres** beyond the side lines of the table.
 
 
 
• **Playing Environment**:
 
 
• The lighting intensity for elite competitions must be at least **1000 lux** uniformly over the whole playing surface.
 
• The floor should not be **light-coloured**, **brightly reflective**, or **slippery**; it is typically made of **wood** or a specialized **synthetic material**.
 
• The **surrounds** (barriers) separating the playing areas must be approximately **75 centimetres** high.

questions.question: The ______ became the 101st World Trade Organisation member to formally accept agreement on fisheries subsidies.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nicaragua**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nicaragua** officially deposited its instrument of acceptance for the **Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies** on **July 19, 2024**.
 
• By submitting its instrument, **Nicaragua** became the **101st World Trade Organisation (WTO) member** to formally accept this landmark global agreement.
 
• The **Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies** was adopted by consensus during the **12th Ministerial Conference (MC12)** held in **Geneva** in June 2022.
 
• For the agreement to enter into force, **two-thirds** of the total **164 WTO members**, which equals **110 countries**, must deposit their instruments of acceptance.
 
• This treaty is the first **multilateral trade agreement** that places **environmental sustainability** at its core by targeting harmful subsidies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Agreement Objectives:**

 
 
• The accord strictly prohibits subsidies for **Illegal, Unreported, and Unregulated (IUU) fishing**.
 
• It bans subsidies for fishing **overfished stocks** and fishing activities in **unregulated high seas**.
 
• It provides **Special and Differential Treatment (S&DT)** for **developing** and **least-developed countries (LDCs)** to help them transition to sustainable practices.
 
 
 
• **Nicaragua Context:**
 
 
• Located in **Central America**, Nicaragua has significant marine interests in both the **Pacific Ocean** and the **Caribbean Sea**.
 
• Its formal acceptance signals a commitment from **developing nations** to safeguard **marine biodiversity** and ensure the long-term viability of the **blue economy**.
 
 
 
• **WTO Ministerial Conferences:**
 
 
• The **13th Ministerial Conference (MC13)** took place in **Abu Dhabi** in early 2024, where members continued negotiations on **Phase 2** of the fisheries agreement to address **overcapacity**.

questions.question: What is Pakistan rank in Global Terrorism Index 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the **Global Terrorism Index (GTI) 2025**, **Pakistan** is ranked as the **second** most impacted country by terrorism globally.
 
• This ranking signifies a deterioration in the security landscape of **Pakistan**, which saw a substantial rise in both the **frequency of attacks** and the number of **fatalities** compared to previous years.
 
• The surge in violence is primarily attributed to heightened activity by militant organizations, most notably the **Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP)** and the **Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA)**.
 
• The report highlights that the provinces of **Khyber Pakhtunkhwa** and **Balochistan** remain the epicenters of conflict, accounting for the vast majority of **terrorist incidents** and deaths in the country.
 
• The **2025 GTI** report reflects data collected and analyzed throughout the preceding year, **2024**, showcasing the evolving threats in the **South Asian** region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Global Terrorism Index (GTI):**

 
 
• The index is an annual report published by the **Institute for Economics and Peace (IEP)**, a global think tank headquartered in **Sydney, Australia**.
 
• It utilizes data from the **Dragonfly Terrorism Tracker** to rank 163 countries based on the multi-dimensional impact of terrorism.
 
• The score is calculated using four indicators: **total incidents**, **fatalities**, **injuries**, and **hostage-taking**, weighted over a five-year period.
 
 
 
• **Other Global Rankings:**
 
 
• **Burkina Faso** retained the **1st** rank in the **GTI 2025**, remaining the country most affected by terrorism in the world for the second year in a row.
 
• The **Sahel region** in Sub-Saharan Africa continues to be the global epicenter of terrorism, accounting for a large percentage of total global **terrorist deaths**.

questions.question: In the World Air Quality Report 2024, what is Pakistan's rank among the most polluted countries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **World Air Quality Report** is an annual analysis provided by **IQAir**, a **Swiss** air quality technology company that monitors **PM2.5** air pollution levels across the globe.
 
• In the **2022 World Air Quality Report** (data often utilized in competitive exams throughout **2023** and early **2024**), **Pakistan** was officially ranked as the **3rd** most polluted country in the world.
 
• During this period, the top two positions were held by **Chad** (1st) and **Iraq** (2nd), making **Pakistan** the most polluted country in the **South Asian** region at that time.
 
• The ranking is determined by the average annual concentration of **PM2.5**, which for **Pakistan** was recorded at approximately **70.9 µg/m³**, nearly 14 times the **WHO** annual air quality guideline value.
 
• The report aggregates data from over **30,000** air quality monitoring stations across **131** countries and territories to provide a comprehensive view of global atmospheric health.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In the most recent **2023 World Air Quality Report**, which was released in **March 2024**, the rankings underwent significant shifts:

 
 
• **Bangladesh** emerged as the most polluted country globally with an average **PM2.5** of **79.9 µg/m³**.
 
• **Pakistan** moved up to the **2nd** position with a concentration of **73.7 µg/m³**.
 
• **India** was ranked as the **3rd** most polluted country, recording an average concentration of **54.4 µg/m³**.
 
• **Lahore**, a major city in **Pakistan**, has frequently been cited as the individual city with the worst air quality index (AQI) during peak pollution months.
 
• **PM2.5** particles are considered particularly dangerous because they are small enough to enter the bloodstream and cause **respiratory** and **cardiovascular** diseases.
